newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Pripps Ringnes says in Swedish Pepsi deal.
newsitem.headline: Pripps Ringnes says in Swedish Pepsi deal.

text.p: Norwegian-Swedish beverage maker Pripps Ringnes said on Monday it reached an agreement with PepsiCo regarding production, distribution and sales of Pepsi-Cola and 7 UP in Sweden starting from 2001.
"Pripps Ringnes will get the full responsibility for these brand names as of January 1, 2001, when PepsiCo's deal with its current Swedish partner expires," Pripps Ringnes said in a statement.
The companies have also started preliminary discussions about possible cooperation in Norway but has so far not reached an agreement, Pripps Ringnes said.

"We've had the ambition to strengthen our portfolio with a strong brand name, our own or an international brand name, within the cola segment," Pripps Ringnes chief executive officer Paul Bergqvist said in the statement, commenting on the Swedish deal.
"Now we have realised that ambition. We are convinced that we will be able to develop Pepsi's position on the Swedish market."
Pripps Ringnes is owned by Norwegian food-based conglomerate Orkla.
PepsiCo is currently cooperating with Swedish family-controlled beverage company Spendrups in Sweden.
